profile.headline: Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
I loved writing code since I was a kid, and I'll probably love it till my dying day. I have worked on a variety of projects from desktop and server-side developer to the frontend, seeking out opportunities to learn new ways of writing and designing code. I see a new technology or an idea as something to interesting to explore and see what comes of it.
I frequently work on multiple feature and product teams. Those that I lead, are made up of developers, QA, product management, and documentation teams. 
I'm always trying to learn. I'm spending most of my time learning and applying React to my current project.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Delivered core features for Google Cloud Backup and DR and Persistent Disk products, spanning UI, control plane, and backend development.

Internal AI evangelist working with developers to improve productivity with prompting strategies and leveraging existing AI tools. 

Built customer-facing management UI in JavaScript, HTML, CSS, improving enterprise backup configuration and management workflows.

Developed control plane services in Go for the Backup Vault feature, enabling secure, compliant storage of customer data.

Engineered new Java-based control plane functionality for Persistent Disk backup & restore, expanding Google Cloud’s disaster recovery capabilities.

Partnered with PMs, UX, and SRE teams to design, launch, and maintain large-scale, highly reliable Google Cloud services.

positions.title: UI Architect
positions.description:
I'm responsible for the overall architecture for the frontend of AGM. This role oversees the general technology direction, security updates, third-party libraries, REST API review, code performance, code reviews, bug triage, and the frontend build system tooling.
I am both a project lead and an individual contributor for several features.
I work daily with several technologies such as React, git, Material-UI, Formik, modern Javascript, gulp, and Backbone.

positions.title: Principal UI Developer
positions.description: I'm developing the client side of a single page web application using Javascript, HTML5 and CSS3 via SCSS. The MVC app is built with JQuery, Backbone, Underscore, Require, Moment and Mustache. Designing and building reusable UI components with an eye toward easy integration throughout the application and maintaining a consistent user experience. Finally, performing demonstrations for internal staff as part of the sprint and also to external customers.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
Developed Harmony's front-end along with a skilled group of developers. Technologies include Tomcat, JBoss, Java, Spring-MVC 3, underscore.js, require.js, JQuery and Thymeleaf. Developed common Thymeleaf tag libraries to ensure common implementation of all forms and other UI components. Designed the web controller tier. Designed and implemented a common approach to time zone management such that time could be displayed according to the customer's preferences, regardless of the time zone they are in. Implemented and managed the localization of most of the user interface.

Designed and acted as tech lead for dynamic content; a way for users to quickly build content sections that change depending upon the email receivers attributes to provide highly targeted email campaigns. This included UI, Spring-base middle tier and backend work.

Designed a drop in replacement for email rendering to render messages faster and make the code easier to maintain.

positions.title: Solutions Architect
positions.description: I have an unusual range of responsibilities that I find very interesting. I work with marketing and engineering to grow the "Developer Community" and adoption for VoltDB. I write blogs, tweets, example code, review documentation, establish meetup criteria, speak at meetups and conferences, and occasionally write new drivers. I produce materials that show how to integrate VoltDB into enterprise applications using examples written in Java, Spring, NodeJS and Javascript though the JSON interface and corresponding benchmarks. It is an unusual departure as I am normally a hands-on developer, but in this case I focus more on how to apply the database into existing applications. I took this job because I felt that I could make a genuine contribution by understanding what customers needed the most from such a database given my background in high scalability web applications. I work with all the teams in the company. My code can be found on Github under the user name Wombat42.

positions.title: Web Architect
positions.description: I was hired by my manager from WebCT to carryon a the HBSP Higher Ed Ecomm site after contractors completed a conversion from the old to new platform. The new version uses RichFaces, JSF, JQuery, JBoss, JBoss Seam, RESTful web services, Oracle EBS, Endeca, Bazaarvoice, EJB 3, Hibernate/JPA, central IT data services, Splunk, Maven and SVN. The role required a lot of hands-on development, working with multiple teams, including marketing, sales, support, product marketing and several third-party developers and services. I was involved in release planning, deployment, overseeing QA, hiring and general technology selections. It was easily the largest and most complicated project, with an excellent team, I have ever been fortunate enough to work on.

positions.title: Senior Web Developer for Harvard Business Publishing
positions.description: Brought on to be a part of the development team delivering a major revision to HBSP's Ecomm site. Was hired as a contractor as a part of budget management. Transitioned to permanent Web Architect shortly after the new year.

positions.title: Principal Engineer
positions.description: This was one of my favorite companies for a number of reasons. I went here to really learn user interface design and was put on a team developing a really amazing OLAP based analytics tool that presented pharmaceutical sales data through a chart generation engine that could export the results to Powerpoint. I was mentored by the VP of engineering and the COO in how to improve my communication, leadership and project management skills through a number of different projects. I led small teams of outsourced developers for various features and a much larger scale project that allowed customers to define analytical units (summary variables and segment groups) through an entirely ajax based UI using what is now Sencha's Ext. The chart generation portion used Ajax4JSF, myfaces, JSF, Hibernate, EJB 2, Maven, SVN and SQL Server. My favorite achievement was the design of a home grown ETL tool based on Ant and JUnit concepts, which broke the ETL process into setup, processing, QA, teardown and recovery steps and the time for each operation was logged the data to an ETL status table. If any part failed, an engineer could cleanup and restart the ETL process at the last successful step rather than starting over from scratch. Logging the performance of each step allowed us to predict how long future ETL operations against similar data would take allowing us to give accurate estimates to our customers when data would become available.

positions.title: CTO, VP of Engineering, co-founder
positions.description: I still felt the work at Empirical Systems had a lot of merit and that proved to be true. Visible Measures started out using nearly the same application from Empirical Systems with significant modifications to the logging and reporting systems. The logging system used a more elaborate file format to greatly compress the size of the logs, cutting transmission time, while not impacting performance. The UI switched from many static pages to an interactive javascript and ajax application. This version could also track Javascript calls in the customer's web pages and send the information back to data collection server that was imported into our DB server. This product used Java, Javascript, Prototype, CSS, HTML, EJB, Ant, SVN, JBoss and a number of other technologies. This role also involved meeting with Angel and VC investors, hiring and strategic management.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: As Emprical Systems was failing, ICI came along and hired me in their professional services organization to develop an editorial workflow platform for developing educational materials. The platform allowed users to import content, tag keywords, create activities and then publish a large XML file that was imported into a Flash compiler. My portion was everything up to the Flash compiler. This project required me to write Javascript, Java, PL/SQL, EJB 2.0, HTML, CSS, Struts, CVS, Ant, FilePro and a home grown connector that imported the FilePro content into Oracle.

positions.title: Founder
positions.description: I was laid off on a Friday from WebCT during the Dot-Com Crash years and started writing code the following Monday. I had an idea for an application analytics platform that could track the features, workflows and errors end users most often ran into. The platform integrated into Java applications through logging statements. The logs were then dispatched to a central reporting server that allowed the developer to see exactly what their customers were doing with the application. The project used Java byte code instrumentation, Java, JBoss, Derby, MySQL, HTML, CSS, JSP and Javascript. While my partner and I were unable to raise financing, the product laid the groundwork for a future company called Visible Measures.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description: I worked on my first real web application here. WebCT produced a very popular learning management platform. I worked on the new enterprise edition, a J2EE based application that was installed at the University's site. It was expected to handle  40,000 or more students, staff and faculty at any given time. It was a SOA based application before prior to SOA being a common name. I was responsible for designing and implementing the security and document management and sharing components running on top of Oracle IFS and 9i. I was also responsible for a component called "Selective Release" which let professors define criteria that a student must meet before being able to view a given content item. I used  Java, Struts, Weblogic, Ant, CVS and EJB 2.0. I maintain relationships with several of my colleagues and have been lucky enough to work with them again in other projects.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: NuMega was a great place where I worked on a variety of challenging problems for pre .Net Window's Automated Error Detection and Profiling products. The company encouraged me to write and get published over 2 dozen times over a period of two years including writing an early Java network development book for MS Press. I was given numerous opportunities to prototype new applications, including NuMega's Java Memory Profiler, which was the first commercial memory profiler for Java. I took that product from prototype to production, leading a team of 4 developers and a QA and a Doc writer. I used technologies and languages such as Java, C/C++, COM, DCOM, both Win16 and Win32 APIs, ODBC, ADO, JNI, JRI and WFC.

publications.title: Network Programming with Microsoft Visual J++ 6.0

patents.title: Distributed capture and aggregation of dynamic application usage information
